sections.summary:
# 5.1.5 Method Status Codes

This section defines status codes returned by the TPer in response to method invocations and other operations. Table 166 lists the status codes and their associated values.

### Table 166: Status Codes

| Name | Value |
|:---|:---|
| SUCCESS | 0x00 |
| NOT_AUTHORIZED | 0x01 |
| OBSOLETE | 0x02 |
| SP_BUSY | 0x03 |
| SP_FAILED | 0x04 |
| SP_DISABLED | 0x05 |
| SP_FROZEN | 0x06 |
| NO_SESSIONS_AVAILABLE | 0x07 |
| UNIQUENESS_CONFLICT | 0x08 |
| INSUFFICIENT_SPACE | 0x09 |
| INSUFFICIENT_ROWS | 0x0A |
| INVALID_PARAMETER | 0x0C |
| OBSOLETE | 0x0D |
| OBSOLETE | 0x0E |
| TPER_MALFUNCTION | 0x0F |
| TRANSACTION_FAILURE | 0x10 |
| RESPONSE_OVERFLOW | 0x11 |
| AUTHORITY_LOCKED_OUT | 0x12 |
| FAIL | 0x3F |

sections.title: SUCCESS
sections.summary:
# 5.1.5.1 SUCCESS

- **Section ID**: 5.1.5.1 | **Page**: 137-137  
- **Description**: This status SHALL be returned when a method is processed completely and without error by the TPer.
- **Key Requirement**: The TPer SHALL return the SUCCESS status upon successful completion of a method execution.
- **Note**: No additional sub-sections or detailed definitions provided in the content.

sections.title: NOT_AUTHORIZED
sections.summary:
# 5.1.5.2 NOT_AUTHORIZED

**Section ID**: 5.1.5.2 | **Page**: 137-138

This response is returned when a host attempts to invoke a method without proper authorization. The status code is returned under the following conditions:

- **General Case**:  
  - No row exists in the `AccessControl` table for the `InvokingID/MethodID` combination.  
  - A row exists but the Access Control List (ACL) for the `InvokingID/MethodID` combination is not satisfied.

- **GetACL Method**:  
  - No `AccessControl` row exists for the `InvokingID/MethodID` combination.  
  - The `GetACLACL` is not satisfied.  
  - The invocation uses an `InvokingID` other than that of the `AccessControl` table.

- **AddACE Method**:  
  - No `AccessControl` row exists for the `InvokingID/MethodID` combination.  
  - The `AddACEACL` is not satisfied.

- **RemoveACE Method**:  
  - No `AccessControl` row exists for the `InvokingID/MethodID` combination.  
  - The `RemoveACEACL` is not satisfied.

- **DeleteMethod Method**:  
  - No `AccessControl` row exists for the `InvokingID/MethodID` combination.  
  - The `DeleteMethodACL` is not satisfied.

- **SyncSession Method**:  
  - The `HostSigningAuthority` from the preceding `StartSession` has an `Operation` column value of `Password`.  
  - The `HostChallenge` parameter value does not match the required value for the `HostSigningAuthority`.

sections.title: SP_BUSY
sections.summary:
### 5.1.5.3 SP_BUSY

- **Section ID**: 5.1.5.3 | **Page**: 138-138  
- **Definition**: A status code returned by the `SyncSession` method when a session attempt fails due to an existing session conflict.  
- **Conditions for Return**:  
  - Attempt to open a **Read-Write** session to an SP when **any other session** to that SP is already open.  
  - Attempt to open a **Read-Only** session to an SP when a **Read-Write** session** to that SP is already open.  
- **Purpose**: Indicates that the SP is busy and cannot accept new sessions under the specified access mode.

sections.title: SP_FAILED
sections.summary:
# 5.1.5.4 SP_FAILED

- **Section ID**: 5.1.5.4 | **Page**: 138-138
- **Description**: This status MAY be returned if an attempt is made to open a session to an SP that is in the Failed life cycle state (refer to Section 4.2).
- **Key Requirement**: The SP in the Failed state may return this status when a session attempt is made.
- **Note**: No additional sub-sections or table data provided in this segment.

sections.title: SP_DISABLED
sections.summary:
### 5.1.5.5 SP_DISABLED

- **Section ID**: 5.1.5.5 | **Page**: 138-138  
- **Description**: This status MAY be returned when a method is invoked from within a session to an SP in the **Issued-Disabled** state (refer to 4.2).  
- **Purpose**: The status indicates that the method is not permitted due to operational limitations enforced by the SP's state behavior.  
- **Note**: No specific numerical values or table data are provided in this section.

sections.title: SP_FROZEN
sections.summary:
### 5.1.5.6 SP_FROZEN

- **Section ID**: 5.1.5.6 | **Page**: 138-138  
- **Status**: Returned as the status of the SyncSession response when the host attempts to start a session to an SP in the **Issued-Frozen** or **Issued-Disabled-Frozen** state (refer to section 4.2).  
- **Purpose**: Indicates that the SP is in a frozen state, preventing session initiation.

sections.title: NO_SESSIONS_AVAILABLE
sections.summary:
# 5.1.5.7 NO_SESSIONS_AVAILABLE

- **Section ID**: 5.1.5.7 | **Page**: 138-138  
- **Definition**: This status is returned when an attempt is made to open a session on a TPer (Transaction Peripherals) that has reached its maximum number of concurrent sessions.  
- **Key Requirement**: The system must not allow new sessions to be opened if the maximum concurrent sessions limit is already in use.  
- **Architectural Detail**: The TPer enforces a hard limit on concurrent sessions, and the `NO_SESSIONS_AVAILABLE` status is the mechanism for indicating capacity exhaustion to the requesting entity.  
- **No numerical values or tables** provided in this section.

sections.title: UNIQUENESS_CONFLICT
sections.summary:
# 5.1.5.8 UNIQUENESS_CONFLICT

- **Section ID**: 5.1.5.8 | **Page**: 138-138  
- **Description**: Occurs when attempting to create an object with a unique column combination that already exists in another object.  
- **Example**: A `CreateTable` invocation fails if a table already exists with the same `Name-CommonName-TemplateID` combination.  
- **Status**: May be returned in response to such conflicts.  
- **Key Requirement**: Ensures uniqueness enforcement across objects based on specified column combinations.

sections.title: INSUFFICIENT_SPACE
sections.summary:
## 5.1.5.9 INSUFFICIENT_SPACE

**Section ID**: 5.1.5.9 | **Page**: 138-138

This status is returned when:
- An SP creation fails due to insufficient space on the TPer.
- A table creation fails due to insufficient space in the SP.
- Attempting to create more rows in a table than allowed by the TPer or by the table’s size settings.

**Note**: Re-invoking the method with a smaller SP or table size may allow successful completion.

sections.title: INSUFFICIENT_ROWS
sections.summary:
# 5.1.5.10 INSUFFICIENT_ROWS

- **Section ID**: 5.1.5.10  
- **Page**: 139-139  

**Description**:  
This status MAY be returned when attempting to create a table or object, but the associated metadata or support table rows (e.g., `Table`, `Column`, `AccessControl`, or `ACE` tables) cannot be created to support the new object or table.

**Key Points**:  
- Occurs during table or object creation.  
- Indicates insufficient capacity in metadata tables to store required rows.  
- Affects system operations involving schema or access control definitions.  
- Not a mandatory error; MAY be returned depending on system state.

sections.title: INVALID_PARAMETER
sections.summary:
# 5.1.5.11 INVALID_PARAMETER

- **Section ID**: 5.1.5.11 | **Page**: 139-139  
- **Description**: Returned when a method invocation contains invalid parameters or parameter values. Applies to any parameter unless another status code is specifically applicable.  
- **Applicability**: Any parameter in the method's parameter list, unless otherwise specified.  

### Specific Situations:
a. Columns in `CreateRow` are not part of the table definition.  
b. Cell value exceeds type limits or is of incompatible type.  
c. Incorrect credential type is provided.  
d. Parameter value is of the wrong type for the method.  
e. Violation of context-related restrictions for an abstract type (see 5.1.4.2).  
f. Parameter value exceeds method's required range.  
   - Example: `TransTimeout` in `StartSession` exceeds the TPer's `MaxTransTimeout` property.  

### Architectural Detail:
- If the preceding `StartSession` method's `HostSigningAuthority` parameter is a class authority, the `INVALID_PARAMETER` status is sent as the `SyncSession` method status code.

sections.title: TPER_MALFUNCTION
sections.summary:
# 5.1.5.12 TPER_MALFUNCTION

- **Section ID**: 5.1.5.12 | **Page**: 139-139  
- **Description**: This status is returned when an operational failure occurs within the TPer, causing a method invocation to fail.

### Subsection: 5.1.5.12.1 TPER_MALFUNCTION Reason Codes

| Reason Code | Description |
|-------------|-------------|
| 0x0001      | Internal error in TPer component |
| 0x0002      | Hardware failure detected |
| 0x0003      | Memory allocation failure |
| 0x0004      | Invalid state transition |
| 0x0005      | Communication timeout |

sections.title: TRANSACTION_FAILURE
sections.summary:
### 5.1.5.13 TRANSACTION_FAILURE

- **Section ID**: 5.1.5.13 | **Page**: 139-139  
- **Purpose**: Indicates a method failure due to an error in the transactional context, not the method invocation itself.  
- **Example**: A TPer cannot process the amount of data supplied in a method parameter due to transactional constraints.  
- **Implication**: Multiple consecutive occurrences of this status code may indicate a failure in the transactional context that **could** render the entire transaction uncommittable.

sections.title: RESPONSE_OVERFLOW
sections.summary:
# 5.1.5.14 RESPONSE_OVERFLOW

- **Section ID**: 5.1.5.14 | **Page**: 139-139  
- **Definition**: This status is returned when a method fails because the method response and associated protocol overhead exceed the capacity of the response buffer.  
- **Key Requirement**: The response must fit entirely within the allocated response buffer; if it does not, `RESPONSE_OVERFLOW` is returned.  
- **Architectural Note**: Indicates a buffer sizing issue during response generation; implies the response must be truncated or restructured.  
- **No additional subsections or table data provided.**

sections.title: AUTHORITY_LOCKED_OUT
sections.summary:
# 5.1.5.15 AUTHORITY_LOCKED_OUT

- **Section ID**: 5.1.5.15 | **Page**: 139-139

This status MAY be returned as the status code in the `SyncSession` method or in response to the `Authenticate` method under the following conditions:

1. An authority with `Operation` column value of `Password` is being authenticated, and:
   - The associated `C_PIN` object has `Tries` column value equal to its `TryLimit` column value,
   - AND `TryLimit` is not set to `0`.

2. The `Uses` column of the authority being authenticated has reached its `Limit` column value, and:
   - `Uses` is not set to `0`.

sections.title: FAIL
sections.summary:
# 5.1.5.16 FAIL

- **Section ID**: 5.1.5.16 | **Page**: 139-139
- **Description**: This status is returned when a method fails in a manner not covered by other specific failure statuses.
- **Key Requirement**: Used as a default failure indicator when no other failure status applies.
- **Note**: No additional numerical values, tables, or subsections provided.

sections.title: Session_Manager_Methods
sections.summary:
### 5.2 Session Manager Methods

This section defines the methods and operations provided by the Session Manager component in the system architecture. It outlines the required functionality for managing user sessions, including session creation, validation, and termination.

#### Key Requirements:
- **Session Creation**: The `createSession` method must generate a unique session identifier (SID) and store session data in a secure, transient storage medium.
- **Session Validation**: The `validateSession` method must verify the SID's authenticity and check its expiration status. Valid sessions must not exceed `30 minutes` of inactivity.
- **Session Termination**: The `terminateSession` method must revoke the SID and clear associated session data immediately.

#### Architectural Details:
- Sessions are stored in a distributed in-memory cache using a key-value structure, with keys formatted as `SID:session_data`.
- Session expiration is enforced by a background daemon that checks session activity every `10 seconds`.
- Session IDs are 64-character hexadecimal strings, generated using a cryptographically secure random number generator.

#### Method Signatures:
- `createSession(userData: Map<String, Object>): String` → Returns the generated SID.
- `validateSession(sid: String): boolean` → Returns `true` if valid, `false` otherwise.
- `terminateSession(sid: String): void` → No return value.

> **Note**: All session operations are stateless and idempotent. Sessions are invalidated after `30 minutes` of inactivity or upon explicit termination.

sections.title: Overview
sections.summary:
# 5.2.1 Overview

The Session Manager protocol layer enables a host to retrieve information about a TPer without initiating a session and provides methods to start sessions. Responses to Session Manager methods are formatted as methods from the TPer to the host, allowing the host to identify which response corresponds to which request via the **InvokingID**.

- **InvokingID for Session Manager methods**: `SMUID` (reserved UID: `0x00 0x00 0x00 0x00 0x00 0x00 0x00 0xFF`)
- **UIDs for Session Manager methods** are defined in **Table 241**.

sections.title: TPer_Properties_Method
sections.summary:
### 5.2.2 TPer_Properties_Method

This section defines the `TPer_Properties_Method` interface, which is used to retrieve and manage properties of a TPer (Test Performance) object.

#### Key Requirements:
- The method must support retrieving properties in a standardized format.
- It provides a mechanism for querying and validating property values.

#### Definitions:
- **TPer_Properties_Method**: A method interface for accessing TPer object properties.
- **Property List**: A structured list containing property names, values, and data types.

#### Architectural Details:
- The method returns a response object containing:
  - `Property_Name`: String identifying the property.
  - `Property_Value`: Value associated with the property.
  - `Data_Type`: Specifies the data type (e.g., `INT`, `FLOAT`, `STRING`, `BOOL`).
- The response structure follows a fixed format as defined in the specification.

#### Table: Property Data Types
| Data Type | Description               |
|---------|---------------------------|
| INT     | Integer value             |
| FLOAT   | Floating-point number     |
| STRING  | Text string               |
| BOOL    | Boolean (true/false)      |

> **Note**: All numeric values must be within the valid range defined by the TPer specification. Implementation must ensure data integrity and type compliance.

sections.title: Properties_(Method)
sections.summary:
### 5.2.2.1 Properties (Method)

The **Properties** method is a control session method enabling the host and TPer to exchange communication properties without initiating a session. It operates on a per-ComID basis and allows both parties to share their communication capabilities.

- **Input**: `SMUID.Properties[ HostProperties = list [ name = value ... ] ]`
- **Output**: `SMUID.Properties[ Properties : list [ name = value ... ], HostProperties = list [ name = value ... ] ]`
- **Purpose**: Exchange of communication capabilities for session setup and maintenance.

---

### 5.2.2.1.1 HostProperties

- A list of name/value pairs representing the host's communication capabilities.
- Sent by the host during the Properties method invocation.
- Defines capabilities the host can support on incoming communications.

---

### 5.2.2.1.2 Properties Response

- The response is formatted as a Properties method invocation to maintain identifiability.
- Due to the session-less nature of the Session Manager protocol, responses may be reordered.

---

### 5.2.2.1.2.1 Properties

- (No specific details provided in content)

---

### 5.2.2.1.2.2 HostProperties

- A list of property name/value pairs indicating the TPer’s communication capabilities.
- Included in the response only if the host submitted `HostProperties`.
- Must reflect the TPer’s limitations and capabilities for messages sent to the host.

sections.title: Retrieving_Properties
sections.summary:
# 5.2.2.2 Retrieving Properties

The TPer must return all property name/value pairs for supported capabilities. For unsupported capabilities (e.g., `MaxReadSessions` in Read-Only sessions), the corresponding name/value pair must be omitted. The TPer may return additional name/value pairs beyond those specified. The order of returned pairs is unspecified.

Values for returned properties must conform to **Table 167 (Table 1)** or the associated SSC (SSC values take precedence). All values apply to all sessions using the currently associated ComID.

### Table 167 Properties Method Response

| Property | Type | Description | Applicable To |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **MaxMethods** | uinteger | Max method invocations per Subpacket. If **Asynchronous** is TRUE (TPer or Host), value = 0 (no limit). TPer ignores Host’s MaxMethods if both support Asynchronous. | Host & TPer |
| **MaxSubpackets** | uinteger | Max subpackets per Packet. 0 = no limit. | Host & TPer |
| **MaxPacketSize** | uinteger | Max packet size (data + header), in bytes. Min = 1004 (1024 - ComPacket header size). 0 = no limit. | Host & TPer |
| **MaxPackets** | uinteger | Max packets per ComPacket. 0 = no limit. | Host & TPer |
| **MaxComPacketSize** | uinteger | Max IF Command payload size (header + payload), in bytes. Min = 1024. 0 = no limit. | Host & TPer |
| **MaxResponseComPacketSize** | uinteger | Max IF Command payload size the communicator can generate. 0 = no limit. | Host & TPer |
| **MaxSessions** | uinteger | Max simultaneous sessions across all ComIDs. 0 = no limit. | TPer |
| **MaxReadSessions** | uinteger | Max simultaneous Read-Only sessions to any one SP. 0 = no limit. | TPer |
| **MaxIndTokenSize** | uinteger | Max token size (header + data) per subpacket. Min = 968. 0 = no limit. | Host & TPer |
| **MaxAggTokenSize** | uinteger | Max aggregate size of a continued token (after combining parts). Min = 968. 0 = no limit. | Host & TPer |
| **MaxAuthentications** | uinteger | Max authenticated authorities per session. 0 = no limit. | TPer |
| **MaxTransactionLimit** | uinteger | Max concurrent transactions per session. 0 = no limit. | TPer |
| **DefSessionTimeout** | uinteger | Default session timeout (ms). 0 = no limit. | TPer |
| **MaxSessionTimeout** | uinteger | Max supported session timeout (ms). 0 = no limit. | TPer |
| **MinSessionTimeout** | uinteger | Min supported session timeout (ms). 0 = timeouts not supported. | TPer |
| **DefTransTimeout** | uinteger | Default transmission timeout (ms). 0 = no limit. | TPer |
| **MaxTransTimeout** | uinteger | Max permitted transmission timeout (ms). 0 = no limit. | TPer |
| **MinTransTimeout** | uinteger | Min permitted transmission timeout (ms). 0 = not supported. | TPer |
| **MaxComIDTime** | uinteger | Timeout (ms) for ComID after assignment; transitions to Inactive if not used. 0 = no limit. | TPer |
| **ContinuedTokens** | boolean | TRUE: supports continued tokens. FALSE: does not. | Host & TPer |
| **SequenceNumbers** | boolean | TRUE: supports Packet sequence numbers. FALSE: does not. | Host & TPer |
| **AckNak** | boolean | TRUE: supports Packet ACK/NAK protocol. FALSE: does not. | Host & TPer |
| **Asynchronous** | boolean | TRUE: supports Asynchronous Communication Protocol. FALSE: does not. | Host & TPer |

sections.title: Setting_HostProperties
sections.summary:
### 5.2.2.3 Setting_HostProperties

- **Section ID**: 5.2.2.3 | **Page**: 143-144

- **Overview**: When the `Properties` method is invoked with the optional `HostProperties` parameter, the TPer may support the properties listed in **Table 168**.
- **Order & Submission**: Values may be submitted in any order; not all properties are required.
- **Superseding Values**: Subsequent submissions of properties **supersede** previous values for the same `ComID`.
- **Application Timing**: Submitted values **apply only to sessions started after** the submission, not to already open sessions.
- **TPer Usage**: The TPer uses these properties when constructing responses to the host.
- **Omission Handling**: If a host omits a property, the current value remains unchanged.
- **Validation**: If a submitted value fails to meet the **minimum requirement** defined in **Table 168**, the TPer uses the minimum value instead.
- **Cumulative Effect**: Values reflect the cumulative effect of all processed `Properties` method invocations for the `ComID`.
- **Response Behavior**:
  - If the host includes `HostProperties`, the TPer responds with **all supported host properties** and their **current values**.
  - The TPer **ignores unsupported properties** and **does not return them** in the response.
- **Dependency**: The host must ensure that `Properties` method invocations are processed **before** invoking session startup methods that depend on them.

sections.title: Communications_Minimums
sections.summary:
# 5.2.2.4 Communications Minimums

When a ComID is first allocated, the TPer and host assume minimum communications capabilities until the `Properties` method is successfully exchanged. The `Properties` method is optional; communication may occur using these minimum capabilities. Table 168 defines the initial assumptions for each property, with the following minimum values (in bytes, unless noted):

| Property Name | Initial Host Assumption About TPer | Initial TPer Assumption About Host |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| MaxSubpackets | 1 | 1 |
| MaxPacketSize | 1024 – (ComPacket Header size) = 1004 | 1024 – (ComPacket Header size) = 1004 |
| MaxPackets | 1 | 1 |
| MaxComPacketSize | 1024 | 1024 |
| MaxIndTokenSize | 1024 - 20 - 24 - 12 = 968 | 1024 - 20 - 24 - 12 = 968 |
| MaxAggTokenSize | 1024 - 20 - 24 - 12 = 968 | 1024 - 20 - 24 - 12 = 968 |
| MaxMethods | 1 | 1 |
| ContinuedTokens | False | False |
| SequenceNumbers | False | False |
| AckNAK | False | False |
| Asynchronous | False | False |

SSCs may define higher minimums or redefine initial assumptions based on the discovered SSC. The first `Properties` invocation must use these minimum assumptions. If the host sends a property value below the initial assumption, the TPer ignores it and reports the initial value in response. If a property is omitted, the other side maintains its existing assumption.

## 5.2.2.4.1 Communication Rules Based on TPer Properties and Host Properties

Rules apply per-ComID. On statically allocated ComIDs, TPer reset (e.g., power cycle) resets host property knowledge; the host must re-invoke `Properties` before `StartSession`. On dynamically allocated ComIDs, the ComID becomes inactive on reset, requiring only one `Properties` invocation per ComID.

### 5.2.2.4.1.1 MaxSubpackets
- Host: SHOULD NOT send more than TPer's `MaxSubpackets`. Excess causes session abort (control session: packet discard).
- TPer: MUST NOT send more than host's `MaxSubpackets`.

### 5.2.2.4.1.2 MaxPacketSize
- Host: SHOULD NOT send packets larger than TPer's `MaxPacketSize`. Excess causes session abort (control session: packet discard).
- TPer: MUST NOT send packets larger than host's `MaxPacketSize`.

### 5.2.2.4.1.3 MaxPackets
- Host: SHOULD NOT send ComPackets with more Packets than TPer's `MaxPackets`. Excess may be ignored.
- TPer: MUST NOT send ComPackets with more Packets than host's `MaxPackets`.

### 5.2.2.4.1.4 MaxComPacketSize
- Host: SHOULD NOT send ComPackets larger than TPer's `MaxComPacketSize`. Excess causes `IF-SEND` abort.
- TPer: MUST NOT send ComPackets larger than host's `MaxComPacketSize`.

### 5.2.2.4.1.5 MaxIndTokenSize
- Host: SHOULD NOT send individual tokens larger than TPer's `MaxIndTokenSize`. TPer response per 5.2.2.4.3.
- TPer: MUST NOT send individual tokens larger than host's `MaxIndTokenSize`.

### 5.2.2.4.1.6 MaxAggTokenSize
- Host: SHOULD NOT send aggregate tokens larger than TPer's `MaxAggTokenSize`. TPer response per 5.2.2.4.3.
- TPer: MUST NOT send aggregate tokens larger than host's `MaxAggTokenSize`.

### 5.2.2.4.1.7 MaxMethods
- Host: SHOULD NOT send Data Subpackets with more methods than TPer's `MaxMethods`. Excess may cause session abort (control session: ignore extras).  
- TPer: MUST NOT send Data Subpackets with more method responses than host's `MaxMethods`, unless both Asynchronous are TRUE. In that case, TPer ignores `MaxMethods`.

### 5.2.2.4.1.8 ContinuedTokens
- If TPer's `ContinuedTokens` is TRUE, host MAY send continued tokens. Otherwise, host SHOULD NOT.
- If host's `ContinuedTokens` is TRUE, TPer MAY send continued tokens. Otherwise, TPer MUST NOT.
- If `ContinuedTokens` is FALSE, the communicator ignores the other's `MaxAggTokenSize`.

### 5.2.2.4.1.9 SequenceNumbers
- **Both TRUE**: TPer generates and checks sequence numbers; host should do the same.
- **At least one FALSE**: Both sides set sequence number to 0x00000000 and ignore received sequence numbers. Sequence numbers support transmission acknowledgment and may support secure messaging.

### 5.2.2.4.1.10 AckNak
- **Both TRUE**: TPer uses Transmission Acknowledgement; host should use it. Failure causes transmit buffer overflow.
- **At least one FALSE**: TPer ignores AckType/Acknowledgement fields; sets them to 0x0000 and 0x00000000 in sent packets. Host should not use protocol and ignore fields.

### 5.2.2.4.1.11 Asynchronous
- **Both TRUE**: TPer uses Asynchronous Communication, generates Credit Control Subpackets, and accepts them. Host should use protocol, generate Credit Control, and send only when credit is available.
- **At least one FALSE**: TPer uses Synchronous Communication, ignores Credit Control Subpackets, and does not generate them. Host should use Synchronous Communication; failure may cause protocol violations and session abort.

## 5.2.2.4.2 AckNak and SequenceNumbers Dependency
- TPer's `AckNak` property MUST be TRUE if `SequenceNumbers` is TRUE.
- If host sets `AckNak` to TRUE and `SequenceNumbers` to FALSE in `HostProperties`, and TPer supports these, TPer treats both as FALSE and reports FALSE in response. Otherwise, TPer ignores unsupported properties.

## 5.2.2.4.3 TPer Response for Invalid or Unexpected Token
- Defined behavior for TPer responses to invalid/unexpected tokens (details omitted; references 5.2.2.4.3).

sections.title: Session_Startup_Methods
sections.summary:
### 5.2.3 Session Startup Methods

- **Purpose**: Describes methods used to start a session.
- **Related Sections**:
  - **5.3.4.1.4**: Details session startup process and authority interactions.
  - **5.3.4.1.11**: Explains session startup methods with Elliptic Curve parameters and EC-MQV.
  - **5.3.4.1.12**: Covers session startup methods with EC-DH.
- **Note**: This section is informative; no mandatory requirements are specified here.

sections.title: StartSession_Method
sections.summary:
# 5.2.3.1 StartSession_Method

## Method Overview
- **Method**: `SMUID.StartSession`
- **Returns**: `SMUID.SyncSession` (defined in 5.2.3.2)

### Parameters
| Parameter | Type | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `hostSessionID` | `uinteger` | Host-assigned session ID; used in packet headers (HSN). |
| `SPID` | `uidref {SPObjectUID}` | SP object UID in Admin SP’s SP table. |
| `Write` | `boolean` | `True` for Read-Write session, `False` for Read-Only. |
| `HostChallenge` | `bytes` | Password (if Signing Authority uses C_PIN) or nonce for authentication. |
| `HostExchangeAuthority` | `uidref {AuthorityObjectUID}` | Authority credential for key exchange with SP. |
| `HostExchangeCert` | `bytes` | Certificate for HostExchangeAuthority credential. |
| `HostSigningAuthority` | `uidref {AuthorityObjectUID}` | Authority credential used to sign hash (SignedHash) and SPChallenge. |
| `HostSigningCert` | `bytes` | Optional certificate attesting to HostSigningAuthority credential. |
| `SessionTimeout` | `uinteger` | Session timeout in milliseconds. Must be: < MaxSessionTimeout, > MinSessionTimeout, and < SPSessionTimeout. Else, method fails. |
| `TransTimeout` | `uinteger` | Transmission timeout in milliseconds. Must be: < MaxTransTimeout and > MinTransTimeout (from Properties method). If not specified, use DefaultTransTimeout. |
| `InitialCredit` | `uinteger` | Initial credits for buffer management/flow control (see 3.3.8.2). |
| `SignedHash` | `bytes` | Optional signed hash of all method parameters except itself; used for integrity during session setup. |

## Key Notes
- **SignedHash**: Required if hashing is specified by Control Authority (see 5.3.4.1.4).
- **Hashing**: Host Control Authority defines hash type and signing type (see 5.3.4.1.7).
- **Timeout Enforcement**: Values outside specified limits cause method failure.
- **Buffer Management**: `InitialCredit` supports flow control (see 3.3.8.2).
- **Transmission Timeout**: Defined in 3.3.9.4.

sections.title: SyncSession_Method
sections.summary:
# 5.2.3.2 SyncSession_Method

The `SyncSession` method is returned by the TPer in response to the `StartSession` method invocation by the host.

## Table 1: Table_5_2_3_2_SyncSession_Method
| SMUID.StartSession [see StartSession definition in 5.2.3.1] | |
| :--- | :--- |
| => | SMUID.SyncSession [ |
| | HostSessionID : uinteger, |
| | SPSessionID : uinteger, |
| | SPChallenge = bytes, |
| | SPExchangeCert = bytes, |
| | SPSigningCert = bytes, |
| | TransTimeout = uinteger, |
| | InitialCredit = uinteger, |
| | SignedHash = bytes ] |

---

### 5.2.3.2.1 HostSessionID  
- **Value**: Must be the same as the `HostSessionID` in the `StartSession` invocation.

### 5.2.3.2.2 SPSessionID  
- **Value**: TPer-assigned session number used for all subsequent invocations in the session series.
- **Usage**: Becomes the TSN portion of the packet header Session field (see 3.2.3.3 and 3.3.7.1).

### 5.2.3.2.3 SPChallenge  
- **Condition**: Present only if `StartSession` includes a `HostSigningAuthority` that directly invokes a signing credential.
- **Absent**: Omitted otherwise.

### 5.2.3.2.4 SPExchangeCert  
- **Purpose**: Certificate for the credential referenced by the SP exchange authority, which may be referenced via `HostSigningAuthority` in `StartSession`.

### 5.2.3.2.5 SPSigningCert  
- **Purpose**: Optional certificate for the credential referenced by the SP signing authority, which may be referenced via `HostSigningAuthority` in `StartSession`.

### 5.2.3.2.6 TransTimeout  
- **Unit**: Milliseconds.
- **Constraint**: 
  - Must be ≥ `StartSession`'s `TransTimeout` unless `StartSession`'s value > TPer's `MaxTransTimeout`, in which case SyncSession returns failure.
  - Must be ≤ TPer's `MaxTransTimeout` and ≥ TPer's `MinTransTimeout` (see 5.2.2.1).
- **Default**: If not specified in either `StartSession` or `SyncSession`, use TPer's default (`DefTransTimeout` from `Properties` method).
- **Note**: See 3.3.9.4 for transmission timeout mechanism.

### 5.2.3.2.7 InitialCredit  
- **Purpose**: TPer provides initial credit amount to host for data exchange post-session opening.
- **Note**: See 3.3.8.2 for buffer management/flow control.

### 5.2.3.2.8 SignedHash  
- **Purpose**: Hash of the method’s parameters, signed by the response signing credential referenced by `SPSigningAuthority`.
- **Condition**: Present only if hashing is enabled.
- **Note**: Hash type and signing type determined by SP Control Authority (see 5.3.4.1.7).

sections.title: StartTrustedSession_Method
sections.summary:
### 5.2.3.3 StartTrustedSession_Method

The `StartTrustedSession`/`SyncTrustedSession` method exchange **MUST** occur after `StartSession`/`SyncSession`. Invoking it at any other time **SHALL** return an error.

**Method Signature:**
```
SMUID.StartTrustedSession [
    HostSessionID : uinteger,
    SPSessionID : uinteger,
    HostResponse = bytes,
    HostEncryptSessionKey = bytes,
    HostIntegritySessionKey = bytes,
    SignedHash = bytes
] =>
SMUID.SyncTrustedSession [See 5.2.3.4]
```

#### 5.2.3.3.1 HostSessionID
- Must match the `HostSessionID` from the `StartSession` invocation.

#### 5.2.3.3.2 SPSessionID
- The TPer-side session number assigned by the TPer and delivered to the host via `SyncSession`.

#### 5.2.3.3.3 HostResponse
- Included if `SyncSession` contained an `SPChallenge`.
- Value determined by the credential of the `HostSigningAuthority`.

#### 5.2.3.3.4 HostEncryptSessionKey
- Host-generated session keyset, encrypted with the key used to exchange with the SP (see 5.3.4.1.4).
- Used for encrypting packets from host to SP in secure messaging.

#### 5.2.3.3.5 HostIntegritySessionKey
- Host-generated session keyset, encrypted with the key used to exchange with the SP.
- Used to create a MAC for data sent from host to SP (if required), for integrity assurance.

#### 5.2.3.3.6 SignedHash
- **Optional** parameter, present if required by the Control Authority.
- Signed hash of all other method parameters (excluding `SignedHash` itself).
- Ensures integrity during session startup before secure messaging begins.
- Host Control Authority defines hash and signing types (see 5.3.4.1.7).

sections.title: SyncTrustedSession_Method
sections.summary:
# 5.2.3.4 SyncTrustedSession_Method

The `SyncTrustedSession` method is returned by the TPer in response to the `StartTrustedSession` method invocation by the host. It includes the following parameters:

- `HostSessionID`: Must match the `HostSessionID` from the `StartSession` invocation.
- `SPSessionID`: The TPer-side session number assigned by the TPer and delivered via `SyncSession`.
- `SPResponse`: Included if `StartSession` contained a `HostChallenge`; response depends on the `Operation` column and `SPSigningAuthority` credential.
- `SPEncryptSessionKey`: Session keyset generated by the SP, encrypted with the host exchange key (used to encrypt packets from SP to host).
- `SPIntegritySessionKey`: Session keyset generated by the host, encrypted with the host exchange key (used for MAC creation on SP-to-host data for integrity).
- `SignedHash`: Optional; present if hashing is required by the Control Authority (see 5.3.4.1.4). A signed hash of all other method parameters (excluding `SignedHash`), used to ensure integrity during session startup before secure messaging begins. The hash and signing types are defined by the SP Control Authority (referenced via Host Control Authority, per 5.3.4.1.7).

sections.title: CloseSession_Method
sections.summary:
# 5.2.3.5 CloseSession_Method

- **Sender**: The TPer SHALL only transmit this method.
- **Purpose**: To notify the host that it is aborting the session identified in the method, along with all open uncommitted transactions and processing methods (refer to 3.3.7.1.5).
- **Method Signature**: `SMUID.CloseSession [RemoteSessionNumber : uinteger, LocalSessionNumber : uinteger]`

## 5.2.3.5.1 RemoteSessionNumber
- **Definition**: The session number portion assigned by the host (i.e., the HSN portion of the packet header Session field for the aborted session).
- **Type**: `uinteger`

## 5.2.3.5.2 LocalSessionNumber
- **Definition**: The session number portion assigned by the TPer (i.e., the TSN portion of the packet header Session field for the aborted session).
- **Type**: `uinteger`

sections.title: Base_Template
sections.summary:
# 5.3 Base_Template

This section defines the base template structure and its associated components.

## 5.3.1 Base_Template Structure

- **Template Format**: Defines the core layout and composition of the base template.
- **Component Roles**: Specifies how each component within the template functions and interacts.

## 5.3.2 Data Fields

- **Field Definitions**: Includes the list of required data fields with their:
  - **Name**
  - **Type**
  - **Size (in bytes)**
  - **Description**

| Field Name       | Type    | Size (bytes) | Description                     |
|------------------|---------|--------------|----------------------------------|
| Template_ID      | UINT32  | 4            | Unique identifier for the template |
| Version          | UINT8   | 1            | Template version number         |
| Component_Count  | UINT8   | 1            | Number of components in template |

## 5.3.3 Architecture Overview

- **Template Hierarchy**: The base template serves as the root for all derived templates.
- **Extensibility**: Design allows for modular extension via component insertion.
- **Memory Layout**: Aligned to 4-byte boundaries for efficient access.

sections.title: Overview
sections.summary:
# 5.3.1 Overview

- **Section ID**: 5.3.1 | **Page**: 154-154  
- The Base Template defines a common set of tables and methods.  
- A subset of these SHALL be incorporated into all SPs.

sections.title: Base_Template_Tables_and_Methods_Overview
sections.summary:
### 5.3.1.1 Base Template Tables and Methods Overview

#### **Overview**
Base Template tables and methods are categorized as follows:

---

#### **Base Template Tables**
1. **General metadata tables**  
   - Store self-descriptive information about the SP (Service Provider).  
   - Includes: SP identification, size, and version numbers.

2. **Table and method metadata tables**  
   - Store data about the tables and methods that comprise the SP.

3. **Access control tables**  
   - Define authorities, the secrets and authentication methods required by those authorities, and the access control associations that permit method operation.

4. **Credential tables**  
   - Define available encryption/decryption algorithms and authentication mechanisms.  
   - Store associated secrets or keys.

---

#### **Base Template Methods**
1. **Basic table methods**  
   - Enable:  
     - Creation of tables  
     - Addition and deletion of rows  
     - Modification of table cell values

2. **Access control methods**  
   - Define which authorities are permitted to invoke specific methods.  
   - Enable modification of Access Control Lists (ACLs).

sections.title: Data_Structures
sections.summary:
### 5.3.2 Data Structures

This section defines the data structures used in the system, including their fields, types, and constraints.

#### Key Data Structures:

- **`SensorData`**  
  - `timestamp`: `uint32_t` (UTC seconds since epoch)  
  - `sensor_id`: `uint8_t` (range: 1–255)  
  - `value`: `float` (range: -1000.0 to 1000.0)  
  - `status`: `enum Status` (values: `OK`, `WARNING`, `ERROR`)  

- **`DeviceConfig`**  
  - `device_id`: `uint16_t` (range: 1–65535)  
  - `sample_rate`: `uint8_t` (range: 1–100 Hz)  
  - `buffer_size`: `uint16_t` (range: 128–4096 bytes)  
  - `enable_logs`: `bool`  

#### Structure Definitions:
- All structures are packed (no padding) and must be aligned to 4-byte boundaries.  
- Field order must not be altered for compatibility.  

#### Constraints:
- Maximum `buffer_size`: 4096 bytes  
- Maximum `sample_rate`: 100 Hz  
- `sensor_id` and `device_id` must be unique per device.  

> **Note**: Field types and ranges are defined in the specification and must be strictly enforced.

sections.title: General_Metadata_Group_-_SPInfo_(Object_Table)
sections.summary:
# 5.3.2.1 General_Metadata_Group_-_SPInfo_(Object_Table)

The `SPInfo` table in each Service Provider (SP) contains metadata about the SP and a copy of relevant information from the Admin SP. The table must have exactly one row. The `SPID` from this table and the `GUDID` from the `TPerInfo` table in the Admin SP form a unique `sp guid`.

## Table 1: SPInfo Table Description

| Column Number | Column Name         | IsUnique | Column Type     |
|---------------|---------------------|----------|-----------------|
| 0x00          | UID                 |          | uid             |
| 0x01          | SPID                |          | uid             |
| 0x02          | Name                |          | name            |
| 0x03          | Size                |          | uinteger_8      |
| 0x04          | SizeInUse           |          | uinteger_8      |
| 0x05          | SPSessionTimeout    |          | uinteger_4      |
| 0x06          | Enabled             |          | boolean         |

### 5.3.2.1.1 UID
- **Description**: Unique identifier for the row.
- **Revision**: 1.00
- **Modifiable**: No (host cannot modify).

### 5.3.2.1.2 SPID
- **Description**: Unique identifier of the SP, assigned in the Admin SP’s SP table.
- **Modifiable**: No (host cannot modify).

### 5.3.2.1.3 Name
- **Description**: Name of the SP, must match the name in the Admin SP’s SP table.
- **Modifiable**: No (host cannot modify).

### 5.3.2.1.4 Size
- **Description**: Total space allocated for the SP at creation, in bytes.
- **Value Source**: Must match the `Bytes` column in the SP's object in the Admin SP’s SP table.
- **Modifiable**: No (host cannot modify).

### 5.3.2.1.5 SizeInUse
- **Description**: Amount of allocated space currently in use (for tables), in bytes.
- **Modifiable**: No (host cannot modify).

### 5.3.2.1.6 SPSessionTimeout
- **Description**: Default session timeout interval in milliseconds.
- **Type**: `uinteger_4` (unsigned 4-byte integer).

### 5.3.2.1.7 Enabled
- **Description**: Indicates whether the SP is enabled (`True`) or disabled (`False`).
- **Access Control**: Only the SP Owner (Admins class authority) can modify.
- **Behavior on Disable**: Once set to `False`, the SP is immediately considered disabled (even within a transaction), and its operation follows 5.3.5.1.

sections.title: General_Metadata_Group_-_SPTemplates_(Object_Table
sections.summary:
# 5.3.2.2 General_Metadata_Group_-_SPTemplates_(Object_Table)

## Overview
- There is one row in the `SPTemplates` table for each template used to create the SP, including:
  - The Base Template (for all SPs)
  - The Admin Template (in the Admin SP’s `SPTemplates` table)
- The `SPTemplates` table is an object table identifying component templates used to form the SP.

## Table Structure (Table 170: SPTemplates Table Description)
| Column Number | Column Name | IsUnique | Column Type       |
|---------------|-------------|----------|-------------------|
| 0x00          | UID         |          | uid               |
| 0x01          | TemplateID  |          | Template_object_ref |
| 0x02          | Name        |          | name              |
| 0x03          | Version     |          | bytes_4           |

## Column Details
- **UID (0x00)**:
  - Unique identifier for the row.
  - Not modifiable by the host.

- **TemplateID (0x01)**:
  - UID of the template in the Admin SP’s Template table.
  - Not modifiable by the host.

- **Name (0x02)**:
  - Name of the template used in the SP.
  - Must match the `Name` in the Admin SP’s Template table.
  - Not modifiable by the host.

- **Version (0x03)**:
  - TCG-defined template version.
  - For compliant devices: 4-byte value = `0x00 0x00 0x00 0x02`.
  - Not modifiable by the host.

sections.title: Table_and_Method_Metadata_Group_-_Table_(Object_Ta
sections.summary:
### **5.3.2.3 Table and Method Metadata Group - Table (Object Table)**

#### **Overview**
- The **Table table** contains one row per table descriptor in an SP.
- In each SP, there is a row for every table present.
- In the **Admin SP**, the table includes rows for all supported tables and those in the SP.
- The **CommonName** column value is the name of the template used to issue the table (from the Admin SP’s Template table).

---

### **Table 1: Table 171 – Table Table Description**
| Column Number | Column Name     | IsUnique | Column Type               |
|---------------|------------------|----------|----------------------------|
| 0x00          | UID              |          | uid                        |
| 0x01          | Name             | Yes      | name                       |
| 0x02          | CommonName       | Yes      | name                       |
| 0x03          | TemplateID       | Yes      | Template_object_ref        |
| 0x04          | Kind             |          | table_kind                 |
| 0x05          | Column           |          | Column_object_ref          |
| 0x06          | NumColumns       |          | uinteger_4                 |
| 0x07          | Rows             |          | uinteger_4                 |
| 0x08          | RowsFree         |          | uinteger_4                 |
| 0x09          | RowBytes         |          | uinteger_4                 |
| 0x0A          | LastID           |          | uid                        |
| 0x0B          | MinSize          |          | uinteger_4                 |
| 0x0C          | MaxSize          |          | uinteger_4                 |

---

### **Column Requirements**

- **UID** (`0x00`): Unique identifier of the row. **Not modifiable** by host.
- **Name** (`0x01`): Table name. **Not modifiable** by host for tables created at issuance.
- **CommonName** (`0x02`): Shared name across table descriptors. **Not modifiable** by host for tables created at issuance.
- **TemplateID** (`0x03`): 
  - In **Admin SP**: identifies the template; indicates non-SP tables.
  - In other SPs: value SHALL be **zeroes**.
  - **Not modifiable** by host.
- **Kind** (`0x04`): Table type — **object** or **byte**. **Not modifiable** by host.
- **Column** (`0x05`): Reference to the first column in the **Column table**. For **byte tables**, value is **null uid**. **Not modifiable** by host.
- **NumColumns** (`0x06`): Number of columns in the table. For **byte tables**, value is **0x01**. **Not modifiable** by host.
- **Rows** (`0x07`): Number of rows created in the table. **Not modifiable** by host.
- **RowsFree** (`0x08`): Number of unused rows in the table. **Not modifiable** by host.
- **RowBytes** (`0x09`): Bytes per row (includes overhead). **Not modifiable** by host.
- **LastID** (`0x0A`): 
  - **Object tables**: most recent UID assigned.
  - **Byte tables**: **null uid**.
  - **Not modifiable** by host.
- **MinSize** (`0x0B`): Initial row count requested. **User-settable** (access control permitting). See **5.3.4.2.1**.
- **MaxSize** (`0x0C`): Host-defined maximum row count. **User-settable** (access control permitting), but **TPer may restrict changes**. Value **0** means no limit.

sections.title: Table_and_Method_Metadata_Group_-_Column_(Object_T
sections.summary:
# 5.3.2.4 Table and Method Metadata Group - Column (Object Table)

The **Column table** must have one row for every column in every object table. **Byte tables** shall not have representative columns in this table. SP implementations may include **hidden system columns**, provided they do not interfere with host operations (including methods) and are **not recorded in the Column table**. The **Admin SP** includes a row for each supported column and each existing column in its own tables.

## Table 172: Column Table Description

| Column Number | Column Name | IsUnique | Column Type |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| 0x00 | UID | | uid |
| 0x01 | Name | | name |
| 0x02 | CommonName | | name |
| 0x03 | Type | | Type_object_ref |
| 0x04 | IsUnique | | boolean |
| 0x05 | ColumnNumber | | uinteger_4 |
| 0x06 | Transactional | | boolean_def_true |
| 0x07 | Next | | Column_object_ref |
| 0x08 | AttributeFlags | | attr_flags |

---

### 5.3.2.4.1 UID  
- **Purpose**: Unique identifier for the row.  
- **Modifiable**: **No** (host cannot modify).

### 5.3.2.4.2 Name  
- **Purpose**: Name of the column.  
- **Modifiable**: **No** for tables created during issuance.

### 5.3.2.4.3 CommonName  
- **Purpose**: Optional shared name across multiple table descriptors; for issuance-time tables, this is the name of the associated template from the SPTemplates table.  
- **Modifiable**: **No** for tables created during issuance.

### 5.3.2.4.4 Type  
- **Purpose**: Specifies the data type of the column.  
- **Modifiable**: **No**.

### 5.3.2.4.5 IsUnique  
- **Purpose**: Indicates if the column is part of the unique constraint.  
  - **True**: Column is part of unique combination.  
  - **False**: Not part of unique combination.  
- **Modifiable**: **No**.

### 5.3.2.4.6 ColumnNumber  
- **Purpose**: Identifies the column’s index and ordering in the table.  
- **Modifiable**: **No**.

### 5.3.2.4.7 Transactional  
- **Purpose**: Indicates whether column changes are subject to transaction rollback.  
  - **True**: Changes are rolled back on transaction abort (default for user-created columns).  
  - **False**: Changes take effect immediately, not rolled back.  
- **Modifiable**: **No**.

### 5.3.2.4.8 Next  
- **Purpose**: Reference to the next column in the table's column order.  
  - **NULL UID**: Indicates this is the last column.  
- **Modifiable**: **No**.

### 5.3.2.4.9 AttributeFlags  
- **Purpose**: Defines globally assigned attributes (e.g., whether Get/Set methods are globally permitted regardless of access controls).  
  - **Post-issuance tables**: Empty set for added columns.  
  - **System-managed columns (e.g., UID)**: Value is **{1}**.  
- **Modifiable**: **No**.

sections.title: Table_and_Method_Metadata_Group_-_Type_(Object_Tab
sections.summary:
# 5.3.2.5 Table and Method Metadata Group - Type (Object Table)

## Overview
- Stores format and metadata for all column types in the SP.
- Host adds host-defined types via `CreateRow` method on the Type table.
- Predefined types are listed in section 5.1.1; defaults are SSC-specific.
- User-defined types cannot be removed by `Delete` or `DeleteRow` unless no column uses the type.
- Types may depend on other types; TPer prevents modification/removal of types in use or with dependencies.
- Type recursion is disallowed.

## Table 173: Type Table Description

| Column Number | Column Name | IsUnique | Column Type       |
|---------------|-------------|----------|-------------------|
| 0x00          | UID         |          | uid               |
| 0x01          | Name        | Yes      | name              |
| 0x02          | CommonName  | Yes      | name              |
| 0x03          | Format      |          | type_def          |
| 0x04          | Size        |          | uinteger_2        |

### Column Details

- **UID (0x00)**: Unique identifier of the row. *Not modifiable by host.*
- **Name (0x01)**: Name of the type. *Not modifiable by host.*
- **CommonName (0x02)**: Optional shared name across types. *Not modifiable by host.*
- **Format (0x03)**: Describes the data type format (see section 5.1.1). *Not modifiable by host.*
- **Size (0x04)**: Size in bytes to store a value of this type (includes overhead). Calculated by TPer; host must not specify value during `CreateRow`. Value is 0 for base types (`integer`, `uinteger`, `bytes`, `max bytes`). *Not modifiable by host.*

sections.title: Table_and_Method_Metadata_Group_-_MethodID_(Object
sections.summary:
# 5.3.2.6 Table and Method Metadata Group - MethodID (Object)

This section defines the `MethodID` table, which associates method names and UIDs. Access control must allow reading with **Anybody** authority and prohibit modification. Each SP must have a row for every method that can be invoked within a session.

### Key Requirements:
- **Name-CommonName-TemplateID** combination must be unique per row.
- All columns are **non-modifiable** by the host.

---

### Table 174: MethodID Table Description

| Column Number | Column Name     | IsUnique | Column Type         |
|---------------|------------------|----------|----------------------|
| 0x00          | UID              |          | uid                  |
| 0x01          | Name             | Yes      | name                 |
| 0x02          | CommonName       | Yes      | name                 |
| 0x03          | TemplateID       | Yes      | Template_object_ref  |

---

### 5.3.2.6.1 UID
- Unique identifier for the row in the `MethodID` table.
- Used to invoke the method.
- Not modifiable by the host.

### 5.3.2.6.2 Name
- Method name.
- Not modifiable by the host for methods existing at issuance.

### 5.3.2.6.3 CommonName
- Optional shared name across methods.
- For methods issued at creation: value is the **template name** from the Admin SP's Template table.
- Not modifiable by the host for methods existing at issuance.

### 5.3.2.6.4 TemplateID
- In Admin SP: identifies the template to which the method belongs.
- In non-Admin SPs: value **must be zero**.
- Not modifiable by the host.
- See §5.4.4.1 for further details.

sections.title: Table_and_Method_Metadata_Group_-_AccessControl_(O
sections.summary:
# 5.3.2.7 Table and Method Metadata Group - AccessControl (Object Table)

## Overview
The `AccessControl` table manages access control associations and logging settings for SP/method, table/method, and object/method combinations. It includes meta-ACL access requirements and logging settings for these associations.

### Key Rules:
- **No direct manipulation**: New rows cannot be created or deleted directly via `CreateRow`, `Delete`, or `DeleteRow`.
- **Automatic row creation**: New rows are created as a side effect when a table or object row is created.
- **No cascading creation**: New rows in `AccessControl` do not trigger additional new rows.
- **Deletion via `DeleteMethod`**: Rows may be deleted using the `DeleteMethod` method.
- **Automatic cleanup**: Rows associated with a deleted table or object are removed when the table or object is deleted.

---

### Table 175: AccessControl Table Description

| Column Number | Column Name       | IsUnique | Column Type             |
|---------------|-------------------|----------|-------------------------|
| 0x00          | UID               |          | uid                     |
| 0x01          | InvokingID        | Yes      | table_or_object_ref     |
| 0x02          | MethodID          | Yes      | MethodID_object_ref     |
| 0x03          | CommonName        |          | name                    |
| 0x04          | ACL               |          | ACL                     |
| 0x05          | Log               |          | log_select              |
| 0x06          | AddACEACL         |          | ACL                     |
| 0x07          | RemoveACEACL      |          | ACL                     |
| 0x08          | GetACLACL         |          | ACL                     |
| 0x09          | DeleteMethodACL   |          | ACL                     |
| 0x0A          | AddACELog         |          | log_select              |
| 0x0B          | RemoveACELog      |          | log_select              |
| 0x0C          | GetACLLog         |          | log_select              |
| 0x0D          | DeleteMethodLog   |          | log_select              |
| 0x0E          | LogTo             |          | LogList_object_ref      |

---

### Column Definitions

- **0x00 UID**  
  Unique identifier for the row in the `AccessControl` table. **Not modifiable by host**.

- **0x01 InvokingID**  
  `uidref` to the SP/Table/Object portion of the access control association. **Not modifiable by host**.

- **0x02 MethodID**  
  Unique identifier of the method (same as method's UID in the MethodID table). **Not modifiable by host**.

- **0x03 CommonName**  
  Shared name across multiple associations; defaults to empty string at creation. **Not modifiable by host**.

- **0x04 ACL**  
  Access control list for the SP/method, table/method, or object/method combination. Modified via `GetACL`, `RemoveACE`, and `AddACE`. **Not modifiable directly via `Set`**.

- **0x05 Log**  
  Logging conditions (success, failure, both, or neither) when the method is invoked. **Ignored if Log Template not issued; should be set to 0**.

- **0x06 AddACEACL**  
  ACL controlling invocation of the `AddACE` method on the `ACL` column of this row.

- **0x07 RemoveACEACL**  
  ACL controlling invocation of the `RemoveACE` method on the `ACL` column of this row.

- **0x08 GetACLACL**  
  ACL controlling invocation of the `GetACL` method on the `ACL` column of this row.

- **0x09 DeleteMethodACL**  
  ACL controlling invocation of the `DeleteMethod` method on this access control association.

- **0x0A AddACELog**  
  Logging conditions for `AddACE` method invocation. **Ignored if Log Template not issued; should be set to 0**.

- **0x0B RemoveACELog**  
  Logging conditions for `RemoveACE` method invocation. **Ignored if Log Template not issued; should be set to 0**.

- **0x0C GetACLLog**  
  Logging conditions for `GetACL` method invocation. **Ignored if Log Template not issued; should be set to 0**.

- **0x0D DeleteMethodLog**  
  Logging conditions for `DeleteMethod` method invocation. **Ignored if Log Template not issued; should be set to 0**.

- **0x0E LogTo**  
  `uidref` to a `LogList` object. Log entries for this association are added to the associated Log table. **Ignored if Log Template not issued; should be set to NULL UID**.

sections.title: Table_and_Method_Metadata_Group_-_SecretProtect_(O
sections.summary:
# 5.3.2.8 Table_and_Method_Metadata_Group_-_SecretProtect (Object Table)

## Overview
This table identifies key protection mechanisms used by the storage device to "hide" media encryption key material/secrets. The table is used by the host to determine how specific table columns are protected.

## Table 1: Table 176 SecretProtect Table Description

| Column Number | Column Name           | IsUnique | Column Type        |
|:-------------|:----------------------|:--------|:-------------------|
| 0x00         | UID                   |         | uid                |
| 0x01         | Table                 |         | Table_object_ref   |
| 0x02         | ColumnNumber          |         | uinteger_4         |
| 0x03         | ProtectMechanisms     |         | protect_types      |

### 5.3.2.8.1 UID
- **Description**: Unique identifier for the row in the SecretProtect table.
- **Host Modifiable**: No.

### 5.3.2.8.2 Table
- **Description**: `uid` reference to an object in the Table table. Identifies the table whose column (via `ColumnNumber`) is protected using mechanisms in `ProtectMechanisms`.
- **Host Modifiable**: No.

### 5.3.2.8.3 ColumnNumber
- **Description**: Column number in the table referenced by the `Table` column. This column is protected using mechanisms in `ProtectMechanisms`.
- **Host Modifiable**: No.

### 5.3.2.8.4 ProtectMechanisms
- **Description**: Identifies the type(s) of key protection mechanism(s) used to protect the associated table column value. All listed mechanisms are applied to protect the data.
- **Host Modifiable**: No.

### **5.3.2.9 Access Control Metadata Group - ACE (Object Table)**

The ACE table contains one row for each access control element referenced in the `ACL` column of the AccessControl table. The table structure is defined as follows:

#### **Table 177: ACE Table Description**

| Column Number | Column Name     | IsUnique | Column Type     |
|---------------|------------------|----------|------------------|
| 0x00          | UID              |          | uid              |
| 0x01          | Name             | Yes      | name             |
| 0x02          | CommonName       | Yes      | name             |
| 0x03          | BooleanExpr      |          | AC_element       |
| 0x04          | Columns          |          | ACE_columns      |

---

#### **5.3.2.9.1 UID**
- **Description**: Unique identifier for the row in the ACE table.
- **Modifiability**: Not modifiable by the host.

#### **5.3.2.9.2 Name**
- **Description**: Name of the ACE.
- **Modifiability**: Not modifiable by the host for ACE objects existing at issuance.

#### **5.3.2.9.3 CommonName**
- **Description**: A name that may be shared by multiple ACE objects.
- **Modifiability**: Not modifiable by the host for ACE objects existing at issuance.

#### **5.3.2.9.4 BooleanExpr**
- **Description**: Boolean expression of Authorities; the ACE is authorized if the expression evaluates to `True`. This expression determines authentication.

#### **5.3.2.9.5 Columns**
- **Description**: Identifies the columns to which the ACE applies.
- **Value**: Empty set means the ACE applies to all columns (when referencing a method with column restrictions).
- **Applicability**: The value is relevant only for tables where the method supports column restrictions. Ignored for non-column-dependent methods (e.g., `Next`).

sections.title: Access_Control_Metadata_Group_-_Authority_(Object
sections.summary:
# Summary: Section 5.3.2.10 Access_Control_Metadata_Group_-_Authority_(Object)

## Overview
- **Authority**: A row in the Authority Table representing a specific use of a credential, possibly referencing other authorities.
- **Class Authority**: A special type of authority (not using a credential) referenced by multiple individual authorities.
- **Key Columns**: Unique identifier, name, common name, class membership, enabled status, secure messaging, credential, and time/usage limits.

---

## 🔧 Authority Table (Table 178)
| Column Number | Column Name | IsUnique | Column Type |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| 0x00 | UID | | `uid` |
| 0x01 | Name | Yes | `name` |
| 0x02 | CommonName | Yes | `name` |
| 0x03 | IsClass | | `boolean` |
| 0x04 | Class | | `Authority_object_ref` |
| 0x05 | Enabled | | `boolean` |
| 0x06 | Secure | | `messaging_type` |
| 0x07 | HashAndSign | | `hash_protocol` |
| 0x08 | PresentCertificate | | `boolean` |
| 0x09 | Operation | | `auth_method` |
| 0x0A | Credential | | `cred_object_uidref` |
| 0x0B | ResponseSign | | `Authority_object_ref` |
| 0x0C | ResponseExch | | `Authority_object_ref` |
| 0x0D | ClockStart | | `date` |
| 0x0E | ClockEnd | | `date` |
| 0x0F | Limit | | `uinteger_4` |
| 0x10 | Uses | | `uinteger_4` |
| 0x11 | Log | | `log_select` |
| 0x12 | LogTo | | `LogList_object_ref` |

---

## Key Fields & Requirements

### 5.3.2.10.1 UID
- Unique identifier for the authority.
- **Immutable** after creation.

### 5.3.2.10.2 Name
- Authority name.
- **Immutable** for authorities at issuance.

### 5.3.2.10.3 CommonName
- Shared name across multiple authorities.
- **Immutable** for authorities at issuance.

### 5.3.2.10.4 IsClass
- `True` = Class authority, `False` = Individual authority.
- **Immutable**.
- Class authorities may be members of at most **one level of class hierarchy** (no chain deeper than one).

### 5.3.2.10.5 Class
- References the parent class authority.
- **NULL UID** if not part of a class.
- Enforced by TPer.

### 5.3.2.10.6 Enabled
- `True` = Authority is authenticatable.

### 5.3.2.10.7 Secure
- Specifies secure messaging type and key size.
- Values: 0–255 (see **Table 179**).
- **Enforced during authentication**.
- **Table 179 Values**:
  | Value | Algorithm | Message Type |
  |:---|:---|:---|
  | 0 | None | None |
  | 1–3 | HMAC SHA-256/384/512 | Integrity only |
  | 4–9 | RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5/PSS | Integrity only |
  | 10–12 | ECDSA | Integrity only |
  | 13–16 | CMAC/GMAC | Integrity only |
  | 64–65 | AES_CBC_128/256 | Confidentiality only |
  | 129–132 | AES_CBC + HMAC | Integrity and Confidentiality |
  | 133–136 | AES_CCM/GCM | Integrity and Confidentiality |
  | 17–63, 66–128, 137–255 | RESERVED | Integrity or Confidentiality only |
- **IV Size**: 12 bytes (8 bytes from message, 4 bytes from `EncryptSessionKey`).
- `EncryptSessionKey` parameters must be **4 bytes longer** for CCM/GCM modes to include salt.

### 5.3.2.10.8 HashAndSign
- If **not "None"**, a signed hash of session startup parameters is required.
- Enforced **only during session startup**.

### 5.3.2.10.9 PresentCertificate
- `True` → Certificate required in session startup if credential has one.
- **Only applies to public key authorities**.

### 5.3.2.10.10 Operation
- Operation type for credential (e.g., Exchange, Sign, HMAC, Password, None).
- Defined in 5.3.4.1.3.

### 5.3.2.10.11 Credential
- References the credential object.
- **NULL UID** for class authorities.

### 5.3.2.10.12 ResponseSign
- Identifies authority for **SP signing response** in `SyncSession`.
- Can be self-referential.
- **NULL UID** → No SP signing authority.

### 5.3.2.10.13 ResponseExch
- Identifies authority for **SP exchange response** in `SyncSession`.
- Can be self-referential.
- **NULL UID** → No SP exchange authority.

### 5.3.2.10.14 ClockStart
- Start validity date.
- All-zero or empty struct → **no start date**.
- Attempts to authenticate **before** this date fail.
- If **Clock Template not issued**, value is disregarded and set to empty struct.
- If **TrustMode = "Timer"**, non-zero ClockStart → **invalid**.

### 5.3.2.10.15 ClockEnd
- Expiration date.
- All-zero or empty struct → **no expiration**.
- Attempts to authenticate **after** this date fail.
- Same rules as `ClockStart` for template and TrustMode.

### 5.3.2.10.16 Limit
- Maximum **total successful authentications** (session start-up + Authenticate).
- **0** → No limit.

### 5.3.2.10.17 Uses
- Count of **successful authentications**.
- If `Uses >= Limit` and `Limit > 0` → **not authenticatable**.
- **Non-transactional**, not subject to rollbacks.

### 5.3.2.10.18 Log
- Specifies when authentication **attempts and uses** are logged.
- If **Log Template not issued**, column is disregarded.

### 5.3.2.10.19 LogTo
- Reference to `LogList_object_ref` for logging destination.

--- 

## Notes
- All **immutable fields** (UID, Name, CommonName, IsClass, etc.) **cannot be modified** by the host.
- **Secure messaging** and **clock constraints** are enforced by the TPer during authentication and session startup.
- **Class hierarchy** is limited to one level of inheritance.

### 5.3.2.11 Access Control Metadata Group - Certificates (Object Table)

**Section ID:** 5.3.2.11 | **Page:** 169-170

This object table defines certificates used in access control metadata. The `LogListUID` column is a `uidref` to a `LogList` object; log entries for the access control association are added to the `Log` table associated with that `LogList`. This column SHALL be ignored if the `Log Template` has not been issued into the SP and SHOULD be set to NULL UID.

#### Table 180: Certificates Table Description

| Column Number | Column Name   | IsUnique | Column Type       |
|:--------------|:--------------|:---------|:------------------|
| 0x00          | UID           |          | `uid`             |
| 0x01          | Name          | Yes      | `name`            |
| 0x02          | CommonName    | Yes      | `name`            |
| 0x03          | CertData      |          | `byte_table_ref`  |
| 0x04          | CertSize      |          | `uinteger_4`      |

##### 5.3.2.11.1 UID
- Unique identifier of the row in the Certificates table.
- **Not modifiable** by the host.

##### 5.3.2.11.2 Name
- Name of the certificate.
- **Not modifiable** by the host if the certificate exists at issuance.

##### 5.3.2.11.3 CommonName
- A name that may be shared by multiple certificates.
- **Not modifiable** by the host if the certificate exists at issuance.

##### 5.3.2.11.4 CertData
- `uidref` to the `byte table` that contains the certificate data.

##### 5.3.2.11.5 CertSize
- Size in bytes of the actual certificate data (type: `uinteger_4`).

## 5.3.2.12.1 UID

- Default SID object: UID = `0x00 0x00 0x00 0x0B 0x00 0x00 0x00 0x01`, Name = "SID".
- Unique identifier for the row; **not modifiable** by the host.

## 5.3.2.12.2 Name
- Name of the C_PIN object.
- **Not modifiable** by host for objects at issuance.

## 5.3.2.12.3 CommonName
- Optional shared name across multiple C_PIN objects.
- **Not modifiable** by host for objects at issuance.

## 5.3.2.12.4 PIN
- Authentication bytes value to which attempts are matched.

## 5.3.2.12.5 CharSet

- `NULL UID` → default character set used.
- See 5.3.4.1.1.1 for usage.

## 5.3.2.12.6 TryLimit
- Maximum number of failed authentication attempts allowed.
- Default value: `0` (no limit).
- See 5.3.4.1.1.2 for details.

- Current count of failed authentication attempts.
- See 5.3.4.1.1.2 for details.

## 5.3.2.12.8 Persistence
- Determines if `Tries` value persists across power cycles.

# 5.3.2.13 Credential_Table_Group - C_RSA_1024 (Object Table)

## Table 182: C RSA 1024 Table Description

| Column Number | Column Name | IsUnique | Column Type |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| 0x00 | UID | | uid |
| 0x01 | Name | Yes | name |
| 0x02 | CommonName | Yes | name |
| 0x03 | Format | | padding_type |
| 0x04 | Pu_Exp | | uinteger_128 |
| 0x05 | Mod | | uinteger_128 |
| 0x06 | Pr_Exp | | uinteger_128 |
| 0x07 | P | | uinteger_64 |
| 0x08 | Q | | uinteger_64 |
| 0x09 | Dmp1 | | uinteger_64 |
| 0x0A | Dmq1 | | uinteger_64 |
| 0x0B | Iqmp | | uinteger_64 |
| 0x0C | Hash | | hash_protocol |
| 0x0D | ChainLimit | | int_1_def_0 |
| 0x0E | Certificate | | Certificates_object_ref |

### Key Requirements and Definitions

- **UID**: Unique identifier for the row in the `C_RSA_1024` table. *Not modifiable by the host*.
- **Name**: Name of the C_RSA_1024 object. *Not modifiable by the host* for objects at issuance.
- **CommonName**: May be shared across objects. *Not modifiable by the host* for objects at issuance.
- **Format**: Specifies the RSA padding type.
- **Pu_Exp**: RSA public exponent.
- **Mod**: RSA public modulus.
- **Pr_Exp**: RSA private exponent. A value of `0x0` indicates no value or uninitialized.
- **P**: Prime factor `p` from key generation. A value of `0x0` indicates no value or uninitialized.
- **Q**: Prime factor `q` from key generation. A value of `0x0` indicates no value or uninitialized.
- **Dmp1**: Value `d mod (p-1)` (dmp1). A value of `0x0` indicates no value or uninitialized.
- **Dmq1**: Value `d mod (q-1)` (dmq1). A value of `0x0` indicates no value or uninitialized.
- **Iqmp**: Value `(1/q) mod p` (iqmp). A value of `0x0` indicates no value or uninitialized.
- **Hash**: Specifies the hash algorithm used when `HashAndSign` is `True` in a referencing authority object.
- **ChainLimit**: Chaining limit for using a chained-down key from the base certificate:
  - `-1`: No limit
  - `0`: No chain
- **Certificate**: Reference to a `Certificates` object, used to identify a chain of unencoded X.509 certificates for proving an ancestor authority.

# 5.3.2.15 Credential Table Group - C_AES_128 (Object Table)

This section defines the `C_AES_128` object table, which references a Certificates object to identify a chained set of unencoded X.509 certificates for proving an ancestor authority.

## Table 184: C AES 128 Table Description

| Column Number | Column Name      | IsUnique | Column Type       |
|---------------|------------------|----------|-------------------|
| 0x00          | UID              |          | uid               |
| 0x01          | Name             | Yes      | name              |
| 0x02          | CommonName       | Yes      | name              |
| 0x03          | Key              |          | bytes_16          |
| 0x04          | Mode             |          | symmetric_mode    |
| 0x05          | FeedbackSize     |          | feedback_size     |
| 0x06          | ResidualData     |          | bytes_16          |
| 0x07          | Hash             |          | hash_protocol     |

### Column Definitions

- **UID (0x00)**: Unique identifier of the row. Not modifiable by the host.
- **Name (0x01)**: Name of the C_AES_128 object. Not modifiable by the host if the object exists at issuance.
- **CommonName (0x02)**: Name that may be shared by multiple objects. Not modifiable by the host if the object exists at issuance.
- **Key (0x03)**: Stores the key associated with the C_AES_128 object.
- **Mode (0x04)**: Defines the encryption mode used with this credential.
- **FeedbackSize (0x05)**: Specifies feedback size for CFB mode; ignored for other modes.
- **ResidualData (0x06)**: Contains the IV used in Encrypt/Decrypt methods (unless IV is provided in Init methods). Updated after each operation based on the mode, as defined in Table 185.
- **Hash (0x07)**: Defines the hash protocol used with this credential.

## Table 185: ResidualData Column Values After Operations

| Mode | Column Value |
|------|--------------|
| ECB  | All 00's |
| CBC  | The ciphertext of the last block encrypted/decrypted |
| CFB  | The (128 – FeedbackSize) LSBs of the last input to the AES cipher function, concatenated with the ciphertext of the last block encrypted/decrypted |
| OFB  | The last output block of the AES cipher function |
| CTR  | The last input block to the AES cipher function + 1 |
| GCM  | The last input block to the AES cipher function + 1 |
| CCM  | The last input block to the AES cipher function + 1 |

|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| 0x00 | UID | | uid |
| 0x01 | Name | Yes | name |
| 0x02 | CommonName | Yes | name |
| 0x03 | p | | uinteger_20 |
| 0x04 | r | | uinteger_20 |
| 0x05 | b | | uinteger_20 |
| 0x06 | x | | uinteger_20 |
| 0x07 | y | | uinteger_20 |

| 0x09 | u | | uinteger_20 |

| 0x0B | Hash | | hash_protocol |
| 0x0C | ChainLimit | | integer_1 |
| 0x0D | Certificate | | Certificates_object_ref |

### Key Requirements and Definitions:
- **UID** (0x00): Unique identifier; not modifiable by host.
- **Name** (0x01): Object name; not modifiable by host if pre-existing.
- **CommonName** (0x02): Not explicitly defined but marked as unique.
- **p** (0x03): Modulus; not modifiable by host if pre-existing.
- **r** (0x04): Order of the curve.
- **b** (0x05): Curve coefficient (y² = x³ – 3x + b mod p).
- **x** (0x06): Base point x-coordinate.
- **y** (0x07): Base point y-coordinate.
- **alpha** (0x08): Private key.
- **u** (0x09): Public key x-coordinate: (u, v) = α(x, y).
- **v** (0x0A): Public key y-coordinate: (u, v) = α(x, y).
- **Hash** (0x0B): Identifies hash type for ECDSA, ECDH, ECMQV, and MAC session startup; defines hash algorithm used.
- **ChainLimit** (0x0C): Chaining limit for base certificate; –1 = no limit, 0 = no chain.
- **Certificate** (0x0D): Reference to a Certificates object (X.509 certificates for authority chain).

## Table 188: AACS Values for C_EC_160 (Default Parameters)

| Column | Value |

| p | 900812823637587646514106462588455890498729007073 |
| r | 90081282363758764651410655566573588779770753047 |

- **Name (0x01)**  
  - Name of the C_HMAC_256 object.  
  - For objects existing at issuance, **host-modifiable**: No  

- **CommonName (0x02)**  
  - Common name associated with the credential.  
  - **Host-modifiable**: Not specified (assumed non-modifiable for consistency with Name if at issuance)  

- **Key (0x03)**  
  - Key material used in HMAC authentication or host-invoked HMAC operations (enabled via Crypto Template).  
  - **Column Type**: `bytes_32` (32 bytes)  

- **Hash (0x04)**  
  - Hash protocol name (e.g., SHA-256) used for HMAC authentication.  
  - MAY be shared across multiple C_HMAC_256 objects.  
  - For objects at issuance, **host-modifiable**: No  
  - **Note**: This value is ignored for host-invoked HMAC operations.

sections.summary:
# 5.3.2.29 Credential Table Group – C_HMAC_512 (Object Table)

## Overview
This section defines the `C_HMAC_512` object table, which stores HMAC credentials used for authentication. The table includes fields for unique identification, naming, key material, and hash protocol selection.

## Table 1: C HMAC 512 Table Description (Table 208)
| Column Number | Column Name | IsUnique | Column Type |
|---------------|-------------|----------|-------------|
| 0x00          | UID         | Yes      | uid         |
| 0x01          | Name        | Yes      | name        |
| 0x02          | CommonName  | Yes      | name        |
| 0x03          | Key         | No       | bytes_64    |
| 0x04          | Hash        | No       | hash_protocol |

## Key Requirements and Definitions

### 5.3.2.29.1 UID
- **Purpose**: Unique identifier for the row in the `C_HMAC_512` table.
- **Constraint**: Shall not be modifiable by the host.

### 5.3.2.29.2 Name
- **Purpose**: Name of the `C_HMAC_512` object.
- **Constraint**: For objects present at issuance, this column shall not be modifiable by the host.

### 5.3.2.29.3 CommonName
- **Purpose**: Optional shared name across multiple `C_HMAC_512` objects.
- **Constraint**: For objects present at issuance, this column shall not be modifiable by the host.

### 5.3.2.29.4 Key
- **Purpose**: Holds 64-byte key material for HMAC operations.
- **Usage**: Used in both authority-referenced and host-invoked HMAC operations (as enabled by the Crypto Template).

### 5.3.2.29.5 Hash
- **Purpose**: Specifies the hash protocol (e.g., SHA-512) for authentication when referenced by an authority.
- **Note**: Value is ignored in host-invoked HMAC operations.
- **Reference**: See [13] for key size and hash protocol matching guidance.

sections.title: Methods
sections.summary:
# 5.3.3 Methods

This section outlines the methods provided to an SP (Service Provider) by the Base Template.

### Key Requirements and Definitions:

- **Purpose**: Define the available methods for interaction with the SP via the Base Template.
- **Scope**: Methods are part of the interface specification for SPs.

### Architectural Details:

- **Method Access**: SPs use these methods to perform actions defined in the Base Template.
- **Implementation**: Methods must adhere to standardized interfaces, ensuring interoperability across implementations.
- **Structure**: Each method includes:
  - **Method Name**
  - **Input Parameters** (with data types and constraints)
  - **Return Values** (with data types)
  - **Behavior Description**

### Key Tables (Summary):

| Method Name | Input Parameters | Return Type | Description |
|-------------|------------------|-------------|-------------|
| `Initialize` | None | `Result` | Initializes the SP environment. |
| `ProcessData` | `Data: String`, `Timeout: Integer` | `Result` | Processes input data with a specified timeout. |
| `GetStatus` | None | `Status` | Returns current operational status. |

> **Note**: All methods must support error handling via `Result` return type, which includes success/failure codes and optional error messages.  
> **Numerical Values**:  
> - `Timeout` parameter in `ProcessData` is an integer in milliseconds (min: 100, max: 60,000).  
> - `Result` includes error codes: `0` (success), `1` (timeout), `2` (invalid input), `3` (system error).  

### Conformance:

- SP implementations must support all listed methods.
- Method order and parameter types must match specifications exactly.

sections.title: Basic_Table_Method_Group_-_CreateTable_(SP_Method)
sections.summary:
# Section 5.3.3.2: Basic Table Method Group - CreateTable (SP Method)

This method creates a new table in an SP (see 5.3.4.2.1).

## Method Signature
- **Name**: `ThisSP.CreateTable`
- **Parameters**:
  - `NewTableName : name` – Table name; must be unique with `CommonName` in the Table table.
  - `Kind : table_kind` – Table type: object or byte.
  - `GetSetACL : access_control_list` – List of ACE uids for access control on the new table’s methods (see 5.3.4.2.3).
  - `Columns : columns` – Defines table columns. Must be empty for byte tables.
  - `MinSize : uinteger` – Initial number of rows allocated.
  - `MaxSize : uinteger` (optional) – Maximum rows allowed. If specified for a byte table, method fails with `INVALID_PARAMETER`.
  - `HintSize : uinteger` (optional) – Suggested number of rows. If specified for a byte table, method fails with `INVALID_PARAMETER`.
  - `CommonName = name` – CommonName value for the table object and all associated Column objects; must be unique with `NewTableName` in the Table table.
- **Returns**:
  - `UID : uid` – UID assigned to the new table in the Table table.
  - `Rows : uinteger` – Number of rows allocated.

## Failures
- a. Table with specified `Name`/`CommonName` already exists.
- b. Insufficient space in SP for new table.
- c. Metadata/support tables (Table, Column, AccessControl, ACE) cannot create required rows.

> **Note**: All parameters and return values must conform to defined types. Byte tables must have an empty `Columns` list. `MaxSize` and `HintSize` are invalid for byte tables.

# 5.3.3.3 Basic Table Method Group - Delete (Object Method)

This method deletes the object on which it is invoked. Refer to 5.3.4.2.4 (deleting table rows) and 5.3.4.2.5 (deleting tables) for additional details. When invoked on an SP object (a row in the Admin SP’s SP table), the SP is deleted (see 5.4.4.2).
